producer_report.summary:
I added the missed behaviors to the firstmate study as cited claims c23-c44 and rebuilt the page. Cargo test, clippy and fmt all pass, and `cargo run -p xtask -- site` succeeds. I could not open the generated page, so I checked it only through the xtask render tests.

The reader's findings held up against the pinned source at 6407052f, with this wording:

- **Reopen:** when the backlog item is still an open captain call, teardown reopens it with the deliverable recorded instead of closing it. `--force` does not change that, and an interrupted cleanup replays the reopen (c23-c25).
- **Yolo:** with yolo on, firstmate merges green, in-scope work itself. With it off, the captain approves every PR merge and local-only landing. A red PR is never merged either way (c26-c30).
- **Places:** only a recorded PR or a cleanup frees a place. Local-only ships and scouts record no PR, so they keep theirs until cleanup. A worker steered back after its PR is not counted again. Secondmates and relaunches take no new place (c31-c36).
- **Local-only, scout, relaunch, secondmate:** each has its own handling.
  - A local-only ship lands by a guarded fast-forward, and teardown also counts work merged into the local default branch as landed (c37, c38).
  - A scout makes a report and no PR, and teardown skips the landed-work check for it (c39).
  - A relaunched ship or scout keeps its recorded harness (c40).
  - A secondmate relaunches differently, has its own recovery path, is never a backlog item, and is retired explicitly (c41-c44).

The model gains a sixth state, `reopened`, and three transitions: `t9` reopen, `t10` yolo merge, `t11` scout done. I also updated `t4`, `t8`, the places-held counter and the concurrency entry. `intro.json` gets matching walkthrough steps, limits, summaries and glossary terms. `findings.json` gains `f3` and `f4`, and `rationales.json` gains `ra5` and `ra6`.

`validation.json` is unchanged because all 18 rules already pass, and the kept test that recomputes it passes. In `site.rs` I only changed a test count (8 to 11 transition summaries), and I added a CHANGELOG entry.

The raw HTML was not inspected.

open_issues: No behavior was run: all new claims are marked read and f4 records that. The new transitions t9-t11 are not failure edges, so the unexercised-path rule does not require a finding for them.
I did not re-derive the 22 existing claims; I only changed c3's text to point to the new place-freeing claims. They still pass the quote check.
The yolo self-merge appears in the model as a ready-to-ready transition (t10) because a merge is not a state of its own.
mistakes: I first skipped claim ids c25 and c34, then split existing claims to fill them so the ids are contiguous.
The first changelog edit failed because the match was not unique; I redid it with more context.
learnings: Each claim quote must be a substring of its cited line range at the pin; I used single-line quotes.
drain.rs has a model-consistency test: a counter named in a retry's `changes` text needs enough transitions in changed_by.
The site renderer needs exactly one summary per transition in intro.json, and an xtask test hardcodes the count (now 11).
xtask/src/site.rs needed only that test-count change; no rendering change was needed.
The source mentions 'handoff' and 'lease', which are banned words here, so I quoted only substrings that avoid them.
Each claim has only the sources I quoted, so a reader should check c32 lines 48-49 together.
